description: Daily 3:15am: when main has something new, update safely (backup first, health check, automatic rollback) and tell your phone the result. Nothing new = nothing happens.
Weekday 7:45am: estate health + resource check to start the day.
Monday 9am: adversarial-ML scorecard + AI-security posture scan.

command: RBI and SEBI cyber/IT regulatory updates this week
description: Saturday 8:30am: autonomous read-only scan of regulator updates (sovereign).

command: Time for your check-in: open the Life OS (two minutes).
description: 7am and 7pm: the Life OS check-in nudge on your phone, through your ntfy alerts (./securax notify setup first).
Sunday 8pm: weekly reminder to export a Guiding Map backup.
Daily 9:05pm: import any AI-chat export dropped into vault/knowledge/inbox (silent when nothing is new).

Daily 8:40am: fetch the RBI and SEBI feeds SILENTLY into vault/regwatch.json. New circulars are not pushed daily (most are not urgent) — the monthly regwatch-digest sends a curated summary, and a genuine deadline shows on the cockpit's Regulatory clock.
1st of the month 8:50am: last month's regulator digest (titles, dates and links only) to your phone.

Every 6 hours: fold old exercise data into totals, remove old versions of images SecuRAX built itself, run the safe clean-ups when space is tight, and alert your phone only if the disk is still short afterwards. Never touches volumes, backups or third-party images.

Mondays 6:35am: confirm every recorded working version can still be restored (its code is pinned in git and its data backup is on disk). Changes nothing; a failure reaches your phone through the andon digest.
Every 15 min: push to your phone ONLY when something turns amber/red, a deadline nears, or it is back to green (silent otherwise; needs SECURAX_NOTIFY_NTFY).

Every night at 2:30am: a verified backup (encrypted if you set a key file); keeps the newest 7, so a week of nights. One day is the most data a lost laptop can cost (doc 84). A stale backup turns the cockpit amber, which the andon reports.
Every night at 2:50am: a verified git bundle of every branch in the backup and off-site folders, and a push to each MIRROR_REMOTES host, so the estate never depends on GitHub alone (doc 84).
The 2nd of each month, 7:20am: prove the code can be rebuilt without GitHub (clone the bundle, check it whole). Changes nothing; a failure reaches your phone through the andon.

command: 15 minutes: update this month's KPIs in Guiding Map, check every KRI against its threshold, and turn any red into one To Do task.
description: 1st of every month 8:50am: the monthly KPI/KRI review nudge (handbook §5-6).

command: Quarterly check-in (about 5 minutes of taps in Guiding Map): grade the quarter, score the wheel, pick up to 3 goals. Then revise the handbook version.
description: 1 Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct 8:55am: the quarterly check-in nudge.

1 Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct 10:05am: the quarterly restore drill. The newest CLEAN backup (off-site first) must decrypt, unpack, match every checksum and open as working data in a scratch restore twin (doc 88); a failure is pushed to your phone by the andon. With no off-site folder it proves the local copy and says so; with no backup at all it fails.

Mondays 9:10am: eight questions that catch an AI that guesses (a false premise, a circular number that does not exist, today's date, a sum). A failure means the model now answering makes things up; the andon pushes it to your phone (doc 89).

Every 5 minutes: is your model machine (a Mac mini or GPU box, REMOTE_OLLAMA_BASE) on? When it goes off, the router is reloaded without it, so nothing waits for it; when it is back, it answers first again. Silent and instant when no such machine is set (doc 90).

Every 10 minutes: this machine shares a card of what it can do (a cloud key? the tunnel? fresh backups? no secrets) with your other machines through sync, so every one of them can check what still works if any machine is off, and so only one of them sends each reminder (doc 91).

9:25am daily: every combination of your machines being on or off is checked; a NEW single point of failure, or a machine that misses far more sync rounds than usual, is pushed to your phone with its fix (doc 91).

Hourly: any routine that newly fails gets a postmortem draft SILENTLY (no phone push for a single blip that self-heals); only one that fails 3 times in 7 days is escalated with the command that starts a fix you approve. Recoveries are recorded for the weekly progress, never pushed (doc 92, signal from noise).
Sunday, before the progress message: the week's after-action review (doc 102) drafted from the estate's own records into vault/mission/: intended, happened, what differed and why, keep, change.

Hourly: the flight rules (doc 102). The autopilot does what it may do alone (a missed backup is retaken, a red disk is cleaned, a core service is healed); anything kept for the owner is only reported.
3:40am: the 2 drills that most need it (never run, longest ago, failed last time, most critical) run by themselves; a failed or much slower recovery reaches your phone (doc 92).
Hourly: disk space, backup headroom, the AI allowance and answer latency are recorded; a trend that crosses its limit within 7 days is pushed to your phone, at most once a day (doc 92).
Sundays 6:40pm: your week with SecuRAX on your phone: your Life OS rhythm, what made the estate stronger, and the one next step (doc 93).

Saturdays 9:10am: ONE calm self-improvement nudge aimed at the Wheel-of-Life area you rated lowest — the single set-and-forget lever that moves it most (doc 112). One signal a week, where it helps you most.

Wednesdays 8:15am: ONE durable idea, aimed at a goal you set (your OKRs, then your weakest Wheel area) — a curated on-device library, never repeating until a theme is exhausted (doc 115). A midweek sharpener, not a feed.

Every 15 minutes: look at every pull request this machine opened; when CI is red, let autobuild fix it (at most 2 rounds, one push each); when it is green and mergeable, merge it and reset the branch (doc 98). Off until you run ./securax ship login, then ./securax routines on pr-watch.
